observations: up.test.sh inherits SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE from the caller's shell: with the README's `export SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=envoy` still exported it fails `expected available webhook forwarding to default to forward mode` (the two resolve_webhook_mode default cases at up.test.sh:121/125 never clear the variable; same shape at main's line 118). `unset SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE` and it passes. Pre-existing, not an acceptance line; remedy is one `unset SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE` (or `SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=` on those two cases) at the top of up.test.sh.

The README block passes XDG_CONFIG_HOME through to `secrets` as well as up.sh: `secrets` reads $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/secretsd/config.toml, so an operator who sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME to relocate envoy.json also relocates secretsd's config and gets `secrets: no secretsd config at …` before up.sh runs. Only affects a deliberately relocated XDG_CONFIG_HOME; the failure variants were driven with `secrets … -- env XDG_CONFIG_HOME=… bash -c …` for that reason.
The rig daemon's process environment carries DISPATCH_TOKEN (deliberate: up.sh's env block at line 620-621); checkpoint 13 scans panes and the private tmux server, not the daemon process, and passed.
